pathway.title: Thor Industries Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: scale and a three-way split across North American towables, North American motorized and Europe cushion any single market, but demand is discretionary and cyclical, so revenue is durable in level and weak in direction. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, with about 36.8% of towable retail registrations and 49.8% of motorhome registrations, and fiscal 2026 net sales were flat at +0.3% although North American towable sales fell 16.1%, because European sales rose 9.0% and motorized sales 12.8%. The order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand is 8.0% higher, but the gain sits in towables at +74.6% while motorized is 27.5% lower, so visibility is uneven. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings are the weakest dimension: reported EBITDA has fallen three years running, by 18.21%, 13.83% and 12.00%, to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, which is 37.98% below fiscal 2023, while net sales are only 4.33% below fiscal 2024. EBITDA margin has compressed from 7.12% to 5.64% as fixed-cost absorption, product mix and tariff-related material costs bite, and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so the run-rate entering fiscal 2027 is lower than the year's total suggests. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K03; calculation K04; calculation K05

Leverage is low and is the main support: total debt is 1.60x reported EBITDA and net debt 0.71x, and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x because debt was repaid and the term loan repriced. The ratio is rising, from 1.50x a year earlier, because EBITDA fell faster than debt, and EBITDA here is calculated from reported lines and includes gains on asset sales and investments; without those gains total debt would be 1.80x, which is the analyst's adjustment and not an issuer figure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07; calculation K08

Liquidity and the maturity profile give a wide buffer: cash of USD 481,988 thousand plus about USD 815,000 thousand of unused asset-based facility availability is USD 1,296,988 thousand, and 98.09% of debt principal falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031. Two limits apply: the facility expires on November 15, 2028, before the notes and the term loan, and its availability follows a borrowing base, and 54.75% of cash sits in Europe, where repatriation to the United States parent may carry withholding tax. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K17

Cash conversion weakened sharply and financial policy did not adjust: free cash flow fell to USD 168,836 thousand, 31.16% of EBITDA against 73.87% a year earlier, while dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of it, so cash fell 17.83%. Term-loan repayment slowed to USD 56,264 thousand, and management itself lists cutting dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are the lever that decides whether leverage drifts up. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

Dealer financing is the largest claim outside debt: standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 3.79x total debt principal and 2.56x cash plus facility availability, one dealer is 13.0% of net sales, and two floor-plan lenders hold about 50% of floored dollars. Settled repurchase losses have been immaterial and the repurchase price is usually below dealer cost with resale value as an offset, so this is a tail exposure that matters only if a large dealer defaults during a downturn. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12

Asset quality adds a non-cash risk: goodwill and amortizable intangibles are 37.39% of total assets and about 80% of goodwill sits in reporting units whose fair value exceeds carrying value by less than 25%, so a modest fall in forecasts could force an impairment that cuts equity and reported earnings but not cash, with its covenant treatment not established. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

Governance risk is medium, not low: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and audit and reporting quality are high, but the proxy statement, credit agreements and indenture are not supplied and payouts exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026, so legal capacity for payouts and guarantor coverage are not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The downside case is a leverage problem, not a liquidity problem: repeating the 37.98% EBITDA decline of the last three years from the fiscal 2026 level gives EBITDA of USD 336,110 thousand and total debt of 2.58x, yet liquidity would still cover a further year of payouts and only small amounts of debt fall due before the facility expires in November 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K19; calculation K20

cells.text: Manufactures towable and motorized recreational vehicles in the United States and Europe and sells them, with parts and accessories, mainly to independent non-franchise dealers; management calls Thor the largest RV maker in the world, a claim that rests on management language and industry statistics

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 3 “Our Company was founded in 1980 and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of recreational vehicles”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 3 “primarily to independent, non-franchise dealers throughout the United States, Canada and Europe”

Three reportable segments: North American towable 33.1% of net sales, North American motorized 25.6%, European 34.3%; the supply businesses in Other were 10.2% before intercompany eliminations of (3.2)%
North America: Airstream, Jayco, Keystone, KZ, Thor Motor Coach and Tiffin Motorhomes; Europe: Erwin Hymer Group with eight primary production locations; supply: Airxcel and Postle

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 3 “Our principal North American recreational vehicle operating subsidiaries are Airstream, Inc.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 5 “EHG manufactures motorized and towable recreational vehicles, including motorcaravans, campervans, urban vehicles and caravans in eight primary RV production locations within Europe”

Independent dealers: about 2,000 dealership locations in the U.S. and Canada and about 1,100 in Europe, two of them company-owned; Thor generally does not finance dealers but gives repurchase agreements to their floor-plan lenders, and two floor-plan lenders hold about 50% of the floored dollars for Thor products

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47 “Two major floor plan financial institutions held approximately 50% of our products’ portion of our independent dealers’ total floored dollars outstanding at July 31, 2026.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 11 “there were approximately 2,000 independent, non-franchise dealership locations carrying our products in the U.S. and Canada and approximately 1,100 dealership locations”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 54 “We generally do not finance dealers directly, but we do provide repurchase agreements to the dealers’ floor plan lenders.”
FreedomRoads, LLC was 13.0% of net sales in fiscal 2026 and 14.0% in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, and 13.0% of trade receivables at July 31, 2026

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12 “One dealer, FreedomRoads, LLC, accounted for approximately 13.0% of our consolidated net sales in fiscal 2026 and for approximately 14.0% and 14.0% in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, respectively.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12 “This dealer also accounted for approximately 13.0% of the Company’s consolidated trade accounts receivable at July 31, 2026 and approximately 14.0% at July 31, 2025.”
Vehicles are built to dealer order; North American capacity can be raised or cut quickly and cheaply, while European changes take longer, cost more and need works council terms for long-term cuts

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 9 “our recreational vehicles in both North America and Europe are generally produced to dealer order”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 9 “Long-term capacity reductions in Europe generally involve agreed-upon terms with the applicable works council”
Motorized output depends on chassis from a limited number of suppliers with no long-term commitments, and chassis cannot easily be substituted
10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 9 “we do depend on a consistent supply of chassis from a limited number of chassis suppliers”
Sales are historically lowest in the second fiscal quarter ending January 31
10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 10 “our recreational vehicle sales are historically lowest during our second fiscal quarter, which ends on January 31 of each year”
USD 3,298,760 thousand at July 31, 2026 against USD 3,055,226 thousand a year earlier (8.0% higher): North American towable up 74.6%, North American motorized down 27.5%, European up 8.4%

Retail share in North America for the six months to June 30, 2026 was about 36.8% for travel trailers and fifth wheels and 49.8% for motorhomes; in Europe 27.0% for motorcaravans and campervans and 16.6% for caravans (industry statistics as quoted by Thor)

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15 “was approximately 36.8% for travel trailers and fifth wheels combined and approximately 49.8% for motorhomes”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15 “was approximately 27.0% for motorcaravans and campervans combined and approximately 16.6% for caravans”
Low barriers to entry and intense competition; principal North American competitors are Forest River and Winnebago Industries

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15 “The recreational vehicle industry is generally characterized by low barriers to entry.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15 “Our primary RV competitors within the North American Towable and North American Motorized segments are Forest River, Inc. and Winnebago Industries, Inc.”

About 34% of fiscal 2026 net sales were in a currency other than the US dollar, mainly euro; international sales, meaning United States exports and sales by foreign subsidiaries outside the United States, were about 39.4% of consolidated sales

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 66 “Approximately 34% of the Company’s consolidated net sales for fiscal 2026 were transacted in a currency other than the U.S. dollar.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 30 “represented approximately 39.4% of THOR’s consolidated sales for fiscal 2026”
About 19,500 full-time employees, about 120 North American employees in certified labor organizations and works councils in Europe; about 23,022,000 square feet of plant and office space

10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 16 “approximately 19,500 full-time employees worldwide”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 16 “approximately 120 of our North American employees were represented by certified labor organizations”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 50 “As of July 31, 2026, worldwide we owned or leased approximately 23,022,000 square feet of total manufacturing plant and office space.”

runs.text: - Low leverage and wide coverage: total debt is 1.60x EBITDA, net debt 0.71x and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x, so another weak year can be absorbed before leverage nears any level of concern, which supports the probability of default assessment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07

- Liquidity and distant maturities: cash of USD 481,988 thousand and about USD 815,000 thousand of facility availability, with 98.09% of principal due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, leave no refinancing wall before the facility expires in November 2028 and support refinancing capacity. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K11

- Scale and segment diversification: the largest North American maker with a European business and a supply arm kept net sales flat at +0.3% while North American towable sales fell 16.1%, which stabilises revenue and cash generation through a segment downturn. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Debt reduction and creditor-neutral refinancing: term-loan repayments of USD 261,264 thousand over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 and margin cuts reduced cash interest paid by 49.51% from fiscal 2024, lowering fixed charges ahead of the earnings decline. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K07; calculation K21

- Reporting quality and no sponsor: unqualified audit opinions, effective internal control and no identified sponsor or controlling holder reduce the risk of misstated figures and of extraction by an owner. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 91; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Falling earnings and margin: EBITDA is down 37.98% from fiscal 2023 and EBITDA margin is 5.64%, so operating deleverage turns a modest sales decline into a larger earnings decline and pushes leverage up even as debt falls. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K02; calculation K04; calculation K15

- Payouts above free cash flow: dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of free cash flow, so cash fell 17.83% and debt reduction slowed, which makes payout restraint the key policy test. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

- Dealer concentration and repurchase obligations: one dealer is 13.0% of net sales and standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 2.56x cash plus availability, a tail claim that would arrive when liquidity is already tested. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12

- Thinly covered goodwill: about 80% of goodwill sits in units with less than 25% headroom, so a forecast cut could trigger an impairment that reduces equity and earnings. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

- Missing creditor documents and a calculated earnings measure: legal capacity, guarantors and covenant definitions are not established and EBITDA includes gains, so leverage is 1.80x without them, which limits how firmly the level of credit quality can be stated. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 88; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K08

In fiscal 2025, we paid a $0.50 per share dividend for each fiscal quarter.”; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52 “The Company’s total remaining authorization for common stock repurchases was $264,174 at July 31, 2026.”

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Thor has no sponsor buyout, recapitalisation or acquisition financing in the evidence: it is a listed company and the four filings state no purchase price, entry multiple, equity contribution or sources and uses to report. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52

Its senior debt was last raised on October 14, 2021, when it issued USD 500,000 thousand of senior unsecured notes due October 15, 2029 and used the proceeds with cash to repay USD 500,000 thousand drawn on the asset-based facility. The notes rank equally with other senior debt and behind secured debt, and the guarantors named in the indenture are not identified in the supplied text. Of USD 875,768 thousand of debt principal, 98.09% falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, so no maturity pressure is scheduled before then, and the loan documents contain restrictions that can limit dividends and new debt. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation A10

On November 15, 2023 the term loan and the asset-based facility were amended: the term loan maturity moved from February 1, 2026 to November 15, 2030, the facility maturity from September 1, 2026 to November 15, 2028 with its size unchanged at USD 1,000,000 thousand, and the issuer recorded USD 14,741 thousand of expense. On July 1, 2024 the margin on the US dollar term loan was cut by 0.50% and the euro margin by 0.25%, with the maturity unchanged. Fiscal 2024 included USD 186,723 thousand of term-loan borrowings against USD 340,619 thousand of repayments around that refinancing, and no new notes or term-loan borrowings were made in fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2026; the asset-based facility was drawn USD 23,216 thousand and repaid USD 23,174 thousand in fiscal 2026, and the issuer states that no borrowings were outstanding at July 31, 2026. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 55

On the equity side, effective July 1, 2026 Thor took full ownership and control of TN-RP, the holding company of the Roadpass Digital business, from its former partner TechNexus under a settlement agreement with immaterial consideration, and moved the operating companies under Airxcel. Net assets acquired were fair valued at USD 94,313 thousand, or USD 93,987 thousand after USD 326 thousand of cash received, which includes the previously held interest, and goodwill of USD 60,922 thousand was recognised. A separate acquisition earlier in fiscal 2026 cost USD 9,250 thousand net of cash in the nine months to April 30, 2026 and added goodwill of USD 10,568 thousand; the business is not named. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A08; calculation A13

After the year end, on September 10, 2026, Thor announced a unified North American RV operation and three operating groups; this is a subsequent event that does not change the fiscal 2026 statements and may change reportable segments from fiscal 2027. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 132

fields.value: | Period scope conflict | The run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period and fiscal 2025 as the prior period, but the sources include the annual report for the year ended July 31, 2026, signed September 22, 2026, which is later than the quarter ended April 30, 2026. The label could also mean the calendar quarter ended September 30, 2026, which no source covers. Showing the April 2026 quarter as current leaves out the later year-end balance sheet, and showing the annual report as current departs from the run setting | Can change a headline figure or period | The run owner confirms the current period; until then every figure carries its fiscal period label and both the July 31, 2026 and April 30, 2026 positions are shown | 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 90 “signed on September 22, 2026”; 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl, page 1 “for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2026” |

fields.value: Source readiness for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the four filings pinned for this run (two annual reports and two quarterly reports) and the run settings, assessed for the selected analytical modules CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The four Thor Industries filings support a credit snapshot built on reported figures, but not covenant, guarantor, ratings or market-pricing conclusions, so creditors should treat any view on those points as unsupported by this evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The annual report for the year ended July 31, 2026, signed September 22, 2026, is the latest and controlling source, yet the run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period, so the period behind every headline figure must be chosen and labelled before leverage or liquidity is called current. The filings print no adjusted EBITDA, so earnings capacity must be rebuilt from reported lines, and the short-term financial obligations on the balance sheet are not explained, which leaves the debt perimeter open. The executed credit agreements and the 2029 notes indenture are not supplied, so security and guarantor terms rest on the filings' own summaries.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the audited annual statements for fiscal 2023 to 2026 and the unaudited interim statements to April 30, 2026 in the four filings supplied, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is low at 1.60x total debt and 0.71x net debt to EBITDA at July 31, 2026, but EBITDA fell for a third year and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so creditors rely on a shrinking earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C12; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity cushions the decline: the asset-based facility had about USD 815 million available at year-end, the first sizeable maturity is the USD 500 million 2029 notes, and cash fell 17.83% over the year while dividends and buybacks exceeded free cash flow. EBITDA is built from reported lines because the issuer prints none, and USD 60,839 thousand of short-term financial obligations sit outside debt; counting them lifts total debt to 1.71x EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation C36; calculation C28; calculation C27; calculation C33; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 93

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt reduction, not earnings, has kept total debt over EBITDA near 1.5x to 1.6x. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,133,915 thousand at July 31, 2024 to USD 922,979 thousand a year later and USD 867,959 thousand at July 31, 2026, as term-loan repayments of USD 205,000 thousand and USD 56,264 thousand were made in fiscal 2025 and 2026, while reported EBITDA fell from USD 714,655 thousand to USD 615,839 thousand and USD 541,912 thousand. The ratio therefore moved only from 1.59x to 1.50x and 1.60x. Repayments slowed sharply in fiscal 2026 while EBITDA kept falling, so another earnings decline without a further paydown would lift leverage; net debt over EBITDA already rose from 0.55x to 0.71x as cash fell and EBITDA declined.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage improved from 8.27x to 10.50x and 12.42x of EBITDA over cash interest, but the gain came from the liability side: cash interest paid fell from USD 86,421 thousand to USD 58,626 thousand and USD 43,633 thousand as the term loan was repaid and repriced, while EBITDA fell. The senior unsecured notes due 2029 pay a fixed coupon and the term loan floats on SOFR and EURIBOR, so cover is sensitive to base rates on the floating term loan and to earnings throughout.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality weakened in fiscal 2026. Operating cash flow fell from USD 577,923 thousand to USD 321,223 thousand, with inventories absorbing USD 73,282 thousand, and free cash flow after purchases of property, plant and equipment was USD 168,836 thousand against USD 454,936 thousand. Dividends and share repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand exceeded it, so cash fell, even with USD 67,875 thousand of asset-sale proceeds in investing flows; free cash flow was 31.16% of EBITDA against 73.87% a year earlier.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate against the debt schedule. Cash plus the issuer-stated unused availability under the asset-based facility was USD 1,296,988 thousand at July 31, 2026 and USD 1,240,176 thousand at January 31, 2026, the lowest cash of the dates shown, when cash was USD 242,176 thousand. Maturities are small until the senior unsecured notes due 2029 (USD 502,814 thousand in fiscal 2030 including other debt) and the term loan due November 15, 2030 (USD 356,219 thousand in fiscal 2031). The facility that supplies the availability expires on November 15, 2028, before either, and its availability follows a borrowing base, with letters of credit outstanding not stated. Its only maintenance test is a springing fixed-charge coverage covenant of 1.0x that applies only when adjusted excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base availability or the commitment and USD 60,000 thousand; the issuer states no reported ratio or headroom, so none is worked out here. Outside debt, standby repurchase obligations on dealer floor-plan financing were USD 3,315,731 thousand at July 31, 2026, of which USD 1,981,105 thousand expires within a year; they are contingent and not in total debt.

fields.value: - Reported EBITDA is calculated in every period because none of the four filings prints EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant EBITDA; this restricts leverage and coverage to a reported, unadjusted basis and leaves covenant EBITDA unknown. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain earnings releases or the compliance definition in the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Other income, net sits inside reported EBITDA and includes gains on disposals and unrealized investment gains that the cash flow statement quantifies only in part (USD 58,931 thousand in fiscal 2026); the rest of the line is not quantified, which restricts the underlying earnings run rate. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the breakdown of other income, net.

fields.value: - Short-term financial obligations of USD 60,839 thousand at July 31, 2026 and USD 60,112 thousand a year earlier have no explanatory note, so whether they are debt-like is not established and they are excluded from total debt; this restricts total debt, net debt and every leverage ratio. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the issuer description of the line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt stack is not drawn: the filings do not state which of the term loan and the asset-based facility are secured, how they rank against the senior unsecured notes or who guarantees them, and the credit agreements and indenture are not supplied; this restricts any statement of structural priority and cumulative leverage. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed agreements, the indenture and the subsidiary list.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, transactions, governance and shareholder behaviour evidenced in the four filings pinned for this run, in US dollars. No sponsor transaction is in scope because none is stated in those filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thor is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the filings supplied, so creditors face the RV cycle and shareholder payouts rather than sponsor extraction, though ownership and board detail sits in a proxy statement not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts are the main governance signal: dividends and share repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand in fiscal 2026 were 132.61% of operating cash flow after capital spending, against 34.90% a year earlier, while the quarterly dividend was still raised to $0.52. Dealer concentration is the main business risk, with one dealer at 13.0% of net sales and standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand on dealer inventory financing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes the extraction and exit-pressure risks of a sponsor-owned credit, but the evidence is the annual report's silence rather than a disclosure of holders. The common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange, the annual report counts only a small number of holders of record, and ownership, directors and related-party dealings are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a holder of 10% or more cannot be ruled out. Certain business combinations that 75% of the directors have not approved need the vote of 75% of the shares, which slows any change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 86

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification support the business risk, but the earnings base is cyclical and weakening in North America. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, and fiscal 2026 net sales split 33.1% North American towable, 25.6% North American motorized and 34.3% European, with a supply business at 10.2% before eliminations. North American towable net sales fell 16.1% and its pre-tax income fell 40.4%, while Europe grew 9.0%, or 3.1% at constant currency, and North American motorized 12.8%, so group net sales rose only 0.3% and pre-tax income fell 19.4% as gross margin narrowed from 14.0% to 12.6%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dealer concentration and repurchase obligations are the largest structural exposure outside debt. One dealer, FreedomRoads, accounted for 13.0% of net sales in fiscal 2026 and 14.0% a year earlier, and for 13.0% of trade receivables, while standby repurchase obligations on dealer inventory financing were USD 3,315,731 thousand, 3.79x total contractual debt principal, and two floor-plan lenders held about 50% of the floored dollars for Thor products. Losses on settled repurchases were not material in fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025 and USD 7,107 thousand in fiscal 2024, so the obligation is contingent, but a floor-plan default by a large dealer in a downturn would become a cash call that the filings do not size by dealer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation A07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is shareholder-oriented but has so far been funded without adding debt. The dividend rose to $0.52 a quarter in October 2025, repurchases rose to USD 115,126 thousand in fiscal 2026 from USD 52,647 thousand, and USD 264,174 thousand of the USD 400,000 thousand authorization remains until July 31, 2027, yet term-loan repayments of USD 205,000 thousand in fiscal 2025 and USD 56,264 thousand in fiscal 2026 reduced debt. Dividends are conditioned on a minimum level of adjusted excess cash availability and a fixed charge coverage test, which the filings do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation A09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fiscal 2026 was the first of the three years shown in which payouts exceeded free cash flow. Dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand compared with USD 168,836 thousand of operating cash flow after capital spending, 132.61% against 34.90% in fiscal 2025 and 42.01% in fiscal 2024, so cash fell by USD 104,608 thousand as operating cash flow dropped to USD 321,223 thousand from USD 577,923 thousand. Of the USD 481,988 thousand of cash at year end, USD 263,889 thousand or 54.75% sat in Europe, so cash within easy reach of the United States parent is smaller than the headline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04; calculation A14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition behaviour is small and not debt-funded, but goodwill is large relative to equity. Business acquisitions cost USD 9,555 thousand net of cash in fiscal 2026, nothing in fiscal 2025 and USD 7,314 thousand in fiscal 2024, and the July 1, 2026 step to full ownership of the Roadpass Digital holding company carried USD 93,987 thousand of net fair value including the previously held interest, with immaterial consideration. Goodwill of USD 1,916,330 thousand plus amortizable intangibles of USD 684,494 thousand is 37.39% of total assets and 61.05% of equity, and about 80% of the goodwill sits in reporting units whose fair value exceeds carrying value by less than 25%, with the valuation of the USD 464 million allocated to Airxcel a critical audit matter. A modest fall in forecasts could therefore force an impairment that reduces equity and earnings without a cash cost, although whether any covenant definition adds back impairments is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation A05; calculation A08; calculation A13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Restructuring is widening and the group is being reorganised, which should improve cost control but weakens period comparability. Restructuring charges rose to USD 58,889 thousand in fiscal 2026 from USD 42,123 thousand across North American towable, motorized, Europe and corporate, and gains on fixed asset sales of USD 36,942 thousand in North American towable partly offset them. On September 10, 2026 Thor announced a unified North American operation and three operating groups, and its reportable segments may change from fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure of financial results is strong but disclosure of creditor terms is thin, so the sponsor and governance risk level is medium, not low. The financial statements and internal control over financial reporting carry unqualified audit opinions, yet the credit agreements, the indenture with its guarantor list, the subsidiary list and the proxy statement are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens, guarantor coverage and related-party dealings cannot be assessed. Medium reflects documented payouts above free cash flow in one year and missing capacity evidence, set against no documented extraction, no described liability management and steady debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the benign view is cash use. In fiscal 2026 payouts exceeded operating cash flow after capital spending by USD 55,055 thousand, cash fell by USD 104,608 thousand, and USD 264,174 thousand of repurchase authority remains while North American towable earnings are falling. If repurchases continued at that pace with operating cash flow near USD 321,223 thousand, the debt reduction that supports creditors would stall, and the unquantified dividend conditions could begin to bind. Against that, management itself lists reducing or ceasing dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are a lever, not a commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A proxy statement showing a holder of 10% or more, or a controlling group, would change the ownership conclusion, and executed credit agreements with wide restricted-payment or investment baskets, or a guarantor group narrower than the operating group, would raise the risk level. Payouts held below free cash flow in fiscal 2027 while the order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand converts to sales would lower it, as would continued term-loan repayment; a repurchase claim from a floor-plan lender would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ownership conclusion of no sponsor or controlling holder rests on the annual report's silence because the proxy statement is not supplied, so a holder of 10% or more would reverse it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens is not assessed because the credit agreements and the indenture are not supplied, so the issuer's summary of payment conditions is the only evidence and actual capacity could be wider or narrower than the payout record implies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The behaviour record covers three fiscal years, so the conclusion that financial policy is creditor-compatible is not tested through a full downturn in which payouts, dealer defaults and repurchase obligations would interact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business acquired in fiscal 2026 for USD 9,555 thousand is not named and no pro forma earnings are given, so the conclusion that acquisition appetite is small rests on cash paid, not on purchase multiples or integration evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Goodwill headroom is disclosed only as a band for several unnamed reporting units, so the impairment-risk conclusion could be milder or sharper once unit-level headroom is known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment comparisons use the fiscal 2026 structure, so a changed reportable-segment structure from fiscal 2027 would break the like-for-like business mix conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thor has no sponsor buyout, recapitalisation or acquisition financing in the evidence: it is a listed company and the four filings state no purchase price, entry multiple, equity contribution or sources and uses to report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Its senior debt was last raised on October 14, 2021, when it issued USD 500,000 thousand of senior unsecured notes due October 15, 2029 and used the proceeds with cash to repay USD 500,000 thousand drawn on the asset-based facility. The notes rank equally with other senior debt and behind secured debt, and the guarantors named in the indenture are not identified in the supplied text. Of USD 875,768 thousand of debt principal, 98.09% falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, so no maturity pressure is scheduled before then, and the loan documents contain restrictions that can limit dividends and new debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation A10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On November 15, 2023 the term loan and the asset-based facility were amended: the term loan maturity moved from February 1, 2026 to November 15, 2030, the facility maturity from September 1, 2026 to November 15, 2028 with its size unchanged at USD 1,000,000 thousand, and the issuer recorded USD 14,741 thousand of expense. On July 1, 2024 the margin on the US dollar term loan was cut by 0.50% and the euro margin by 0.25%, with the maturity unchanged. Fiscal 2024 included USD 186,723 thousand of term-loan borrowings against USD 340,619 thousand of repayments around that refinancing, and no new notes or term-loan borrowings were made in fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2026; the asset-based facility was drawn USD 23,216 thousand and repaid USD 23,174 thousand in fiscal 2026, and the issuer states that no borrowings were outstanding at July 31, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 55

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the equity side, effective July 1, 2026 Thor took full ownership and control of TN-RP, the holding company of the Roadpass Digital business, from its former partner TechNexus under a settlement agreement with immaterial consideration, and moved the operating companies under Airxcel. Net assets acquired were fair valued at USD 94,313 thousand, or USD 93,987 thousand after USD 326 thousand of cash received, which includes the previously held interest, and goodwill of USD 60,922 thousand was recognised. A separate acquisition earlier in fiscal 2026 cost USD 9,250 thousand net of cash in the nine months to April 30, 2026 and added goodwill of USD 10,568 thousand; the business is not named.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A08; calculation A13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the year end, on September 10, 2026, Thor announced a unified North American RV operation and three operating groups; this is a subsequent event that does not change the fiscal 2026 statements and may change reportable segments from fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by payouts that exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and by missing evidence on legal capacity, because shareholder returns compete with debt reduction when earnings fall and unseen documents may allow wider payouts, which implies watching cash use rather than assuming sponsor-style extraction. Countervailing evidence is the record of debt repayment, maturity extensions, margin cuts and no described liability management.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated fundamental credit view built from the four pinned filings and the three supplied module outputs, in US dollars. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thor's low leverage, large liquidity and distant maturities protect creditors through another weak year, but earnings have fallen three years running and payouts now exceed free cash flow, so the trend, not the level, is the risk to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA fell 12.00% to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, lifting total debt to EBITDA from 1.50x to 1.60x, yet cash plus unused facility availability of USD 1,296,988 thousand is 5.79x one year of payouts and 98.09% of debt principal falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031. Cash use is the swing factor: dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand exceeded free cash flow of USD 168,836 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K06; calculation K09; calculation K10; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: scale and a three-way split across North American towables, North American motorized and Europe cushion any single market, but demand is discretionary and cyclical, so revenue is durable in level and weak in direction. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, with about 36.8% of towable retail registrations and 49.8% of motorhome registrations, and fiscal 2026 net sales were flat at +0.3% although North American towable sales fell 16.1%, because European sales rose 9.0% and motorized sales 12.8%. The order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand is 8.0% higher, but the gain sits in towables at +74.6% while motorized is 27.5% lower, so visibility is uneven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are the weakest dimension: reported EBITDA has fallen three years running, by 18.21%, 13.83% and 12.00%, to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, which is 37.98% below fiscal 2023, while net sales are only 4.33% below fiscal 2024. EBITDA margin has compressed from 7.12% to 5.64% as fixed-cost absorption, product mix and tariff-related material costs bite, and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so the run-rate entering fiscal 2027 is lower than the year's total suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K03; calculation K04; calculation K05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is low and is the main support: total debt is 1.60x reported EBITDA and net debt 0.71x, and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x because debt was repaid and the term loan repriced. The ratio is rising, from 1.50x a year earlier, because EBITDA fell faster than debt, and EBITDA here is calculated from reported lines and includes gains on asset sales and investments; without those gains total debt would be 1.80x, which is the analyst's adjustment and not an issuer figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07; calculation K08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile give a wide buffer: cash of USD 481,988 thousand plus about USD 815,000 thousand of unused asset-based facility availability is USD 1,296,988 thousand, and 98.09% of debt principal falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031. Two limits apply: the facility expires on November 15, 2028, before the notes and the term loan, and its availability follows a borrowing base, and 54.75% of cash sits in Europe, where repatriation to the United States parent may carry withholding tax.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion weakened sharply and financial policy did not adjust: free cash flow fell to USD 168,836 thousand, 31.16% of EBITDA against 73.87% a year earlier, while dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of it, so cash fell 17.83%. Term-loan repayment slowed to USD 56,264 thousand, and management itself lists cutting dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are the lever that decides whether leverage drifts up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dealer financing is the largest claim outside debt: standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 3.79x total debt principal and 2.56x cash plus facility availability, one dealer is 13.0% of net sales, and two floor-plan lenders hold about 50% of floored dollars. Settled repurchase losses have been immaterial and the repurchase price is usually below dealer cost with resale value as an offset, so this is a tail exposure that matters only if a large dealer defaults during a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset quality adds a non-cash risk: goodwill and amortizable intangibles are 37.39% of total assets and about 80% of goodwill sits in reporting units whose fair value exceeds carrying value by less than 25%, so a modest fall in forecasts could force an impairment that cuts equity and reported earnings but not cash, with its covenant treatment not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium, not low: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and audit and reporting quality are high, but the proxy statement, credit agreements and indenture are not supplied and payouts exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026, so legal capacity for payouts and guarantor coverage are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside case is a leverage problem, not a liquidity problem: repeating the 37.98% EBITDA decline of the last three years from the fiscal 2026 level gives EBITDA of USD 336,110 thousand and total debt of 2.58x, yet liquidity would still cover a further year of payouts and only small amounts of debt fall due before the facility expires in November 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K19; calculation K20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against comfort in the level of credit quality is the trend. Fiscal fourth-quarter EBITDA was 42.17% below the prior year on net sales 8.41% lower, and four times that quarter, USD 520,016 thousand, would already put total debt at 1.67x EBITDA. North American motorized backlog fell 27.5%, and management expects the rest of calendar 2026 and possibly beyond to stay under pressure from interest rates, tariffs and fuel prices linked to disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, so a further decline is plausible rather than remote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 58; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K05; calculation K18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A stable or rising EBITDA with a margin above 5.64%, while the towable backlog converts and tariff refunds are received, would lift the earnings assessment, and payouts held below free cash flow would remove the policy concern. Total debt above 2.00x EBITDA, which is the analyst's own tripwire and not a covenant, cash plus availability below the January 31, 2026 low of USD 1,240,176 thousand, or a dealer credit event that triggers repurchase demands would move the view down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 60; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K04; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA is calculated from statement lines because no source prints it, so every leverage and coverage conclusion is on a reported, unadjusted basis and a lender definition could move the ratios in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom, guarantor coverage, security and payout capacity cannot be tested because the credit agreements, the indenture and the subsidiary list are not supplied, so structural priority, recovery and legal-capacity conclusions lie outside this view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside case applies the observed fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 EBITDA decline to the current year and holds capital spending, interest, working capital and the effective tax rate at fiscal 2026 levels, so its leverage and cash figures are sensitivities and not forecasts.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation K19; calculation K20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, market prices, peer set or portfolio limits are supplied, so the conclusions on market access and standing against other issuers rest on disclosed fair values and company statements only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fourth-quarter figures are derived as the year less nine months and no balance sheet at October 31, 2025 is supplied, so the 42.17% fourth-quarter EBITDA fall that drives the run-rate conclusion is a calculated figure and not a reported one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low leverage and wide coverage: total debt is 1.60x EBITDA, net debt 0.71x and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x, so another weak year can be absorbed before leverage nears any level of concern, which supports the probability of default assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and distant maturities: cash of USD 481,988 thousand and about USD 815,000 thousand of facility availability, with 98.09% of principal due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, leave no refinancing wall before the facility expires in November 2028 and support refinancing capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and segment diversification: the largest North American maker with a European business and a supply arm kept net sales flat at +0.3% while North American towable sales fell 16.1%, which stabilises revenue and cash generation through a segment downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt reduction and creditor-neutral refinancing: term-loan repayments of USD 261,264 thousand over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 and margin cuts reduced cash interest paid by 49.51% from fiscal 2024, lowering fixed charges ahead of the earnings decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K07; calculation K21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reporting quality and no sponsor: unqualified audit opinions, effective internal control and no identified sponsor or controlling holder reduce the risk of misstated figures and of extraction by an owner.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Falling earnings and margin: EBITDA is down 37.98% from fiscal 2023 and EBITDA margin is 5.64%, so operating deleverage turns a modest sales decline into a larger earnings decline and pushes leverage up even as debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K02; calculation K04; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payouts above free cash flow: dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of free cash flow, so cash fell 17.83% and debt reduction slowed, which makes payout restraint the key policy test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Dealer concentration and repurchase obligations: one dealer is 13.0% of net sales and standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 2.56x cash plus availability, a tail claim that would arrive when liquidity is already tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Thinly covered goodwill: about 80% of goodwill sits in units with less than 25% headroom, so a forecast cut could trigger an impairment that reduces equity and earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Missing creditor documents and a calculated earnings measure: legal capacity, guarantors and covenant definitions are not established and EBITDA includes gains, so leverage is 1.80x without them, which limits how firmly the level of credit quality can be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 88; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thor is a listed manufacturer with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the creditor question is financial policy rather than owner behaviour. It states that it is the sole owner of its operating subsidiaries, which sit in three groups: North American towables and motorized brands, the Erwin Hymer Group in Europe, and the Airxcel and Postle supply businesses, and on July 1, 2026 it took full control of the Roadpass Digital holding company, now under Airxcel. The notes carry guarantees from subsidiaries that are not named in the supplied text, and more than half of cash is held in Europe, so whether the parent and the guarantors can reach the cash and earnings of the European group is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium: payouts that exceeded free cash flow in one year and missing capacity evidence, against no described liability management, steady debt reduction and maturity extensions with unchanged covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional, discretionary and cyclical rather than recurring: vehicles are built to dealer order, sold to independent dealers who finance inventory with floor-plan lenders, and volume follows consumer confidence and interest rates. In fiscal 2026 shipments fell 11.8% in total and 20.7% in North American towables, while price and mix added 4.6% per unit in towables, so net sales held up through motorized volume, mix and the euro rather than towable demand. Visibility comes from the order backlog, which equals 34.33% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and from one dealer at 13.0% of sales whose bargaining power rises as dealers consolidate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation K16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is limited: management chose not to pass on all cost increases including tariff costs in fiscal 2026 to protect dealer and consumer affordability, which keeps revenue in the short term but gives up margin, and sensitivity to interest rates, fuel prices and tariffs is high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defended only partly under volume pressure. Material, labour, freight and warranty costs are the main costs, and in North American towables cost of sales rose to 88.8% of net sales from 86.9% as overhead absorption worsened with lower volume, which is why pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales. North American capacity can be cut quickly, but European reductions need works council agreements and bring negotiated separation costs, and restructuring charges rose to USD 58,889 thousand in fiscal 2026 across all segments. Selling, general and administrative expense eased 2.1% mainly through lower incentive pay, a cushion that shrinks as profit falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 129; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts weakly into free cash flow in fiscal 2026: 31.16% against 73.87% a year earlier, because operating cash flow fell to USD 321,223 thousand with USD 73,282 thousand absorbed by inventory while capital spending rose to USD 152,387 thousand. Capital spending equals 28.12% of EBITDA and USD 175,000 thousand is committed for fiscal 2027 to be funded from operations; the split between maintenance and growth is not disclosed, so the flexible part is unknown. Cash interest of USD 43,633 thousand is low and falling, and cash taxes of USD 61,802 thousand moved with profit, so the cash cost of debt is not the pressure point; inventory, capital spending and payouts are.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K09; calculation K22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and entry is easy: about 80 manufacturers compete in the United States and Canada, the principal rivals are Forest River and Winnebago Industries, and the industry has low barriers to entry, so share and price are contested and pricing power is limited. Buyer power is high because one consolidating dealer is 13.0% of sales and two floor-plan lenders decide how much inventory dealers can carry, which can cut orders quickly. Supplier power is concentrated in chassis, where a limited number of suppliers allocate supply in shortages and chassis cannot easily be substituted, and substitutes include used vehicles and other leisure spending, which gain in downturns. Each force acts on volume and margin, not on solvency, and Thor's scale and low leverage let it absorb more of that pressure than a smaller maker.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and policy factors do alter credit quality here. Tariffs raised component costs that were not fully passed on, a court ruling opened a refund process for tariffs paid under one authority, and a temporary global tariff expired in late July 2026, so net tariff cost is uncertain and refunds could help cash. Interest rates and consumer confidence drive retail demand and dealer carrying costs, fuel prices linked to the Iran conflict may hurt retail demand, emissions rules reach Thor through chassis makers, and new European limits on formaldehyde emissions phase in from calendar 2026 and 2027, which can raise product cost. Currency matters because about 34% of sales are in euros and other currencies and the euro term loan is an economic hedge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths and weaknesses are ranked above. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand converting to sales, possible refunds of tariffs paid, restructuring savings that lift margin, and a European retail market that grew 2.6% in motorcaravans and campervans in the first half of calendar 2026, where Thor gained 7.2%. Threats that could weaken credit quality are a further fall in North American towable retail demand, new tariffs or higher fuel prices, a dealer financing squeeze if floor-plan lenders pull back, chassis shortages, and an impairment of thinly covered goodwill.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are low leverage, wide coverage, USD 1,296,988 thousand of liquidity and long-dated debt; the constraints are falling and thin margins, weak cash conversion, payouts above free cash flow and contingent dealer claims. The trend is negative on earnings and cash flow and neutral to positive on debt, with total debt falling from USD 1,133,915 thousand in fiscal 2024 to USD 867,959 thousand in fiscal 2026. Access to capital markets is untested in the evidence, but the senior unsecured notes carry a fair value of 93.00% of principal and the term loan 100.43%, so the issuer is not priced as distressed on the issuer's own fair value disclosure. Missing datapoints that would firm up the view are the credit agreements, covenant headroom, guarantor coverage, ratings, market prices, unit-level goodwill headroom and dealer-level repurchase exposure.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 119; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K13; calculation K23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the headwinds dominate in North America and the tailwinds sit in Europe and the backlog. The industry association forecasts calendar 2026 North American wholesale shipments of about 314,000 units, 8.2% lower, within a range of 300,000 to 328,100 units, and first-half industry towable retail registrations fell 15.5% while Thor's fell 20.2%, so Thor lost share in towables while dealer inventories fell 12.7% to about 64,000 units and may restock only slowly. In Europe management expects stable volume but pressure on prices and margins, and for the group it plans capital spending of USD 175,000 thousand in fiscal 2027. Over three to five years management remains optimistic about long-term retail demand, a view that is management language and not tested here; the credit event in that window is refinancing the facility in 2028 and USD 859,033 thousand of debt, mostly the notes and the term loan, in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, which low leverage and liquidity make manageable if EBITDA stabilises.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is another leg down in North American towable retail demand from high borrowing costs, tariffs and fuel prices, with dealers destocking faster than retail, as in fiscal 2026 when company wholesale units fell 20.5% against retail registrations down 18.5%. The first operational break is operating deleverage in towables, where pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales, and the second is a European margin squeeze. If EBITDA repeated the 37.98% fall of fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 from its fiscal 2026 level it would be USD 336,110 thousand, EBITDA margin 3.50%, total debt 2.58x EBITDA and EBITDA 7.70x cash interest; the milder run-rate case of four times the fourth quarter gives USD 520,016 thousand and 1.67x. With capital spending, interest and working capital unchanged and the effective tax rate at 26.8%, free cash flow in the stress case falls to about USD 18,189 thousand, so payouts at the fiscal 2026 level would draw about USD 205,702 thousand of cash and leave about USD 276,286 thousand, while the facility, undrawn at year end, still adds availability subject to its borrowing base, which shrinks with receivables and inventory.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are cutting repurchases and dividends, which management lists as responses to a shortfall, reducing capital spending, lowering incentive pay and extending restructuring, and these are enough to avoid a liquidity event in the case shown. The credit event that the levers do not address is a dealer default that triggers repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand gross, which is 2.56x liquidity before resale value, and the springing fixed-charge covenant of the facility applies only if excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base or facility size and USD 60,000 thousand. Default is not the base case: nothing in the evidence points to one, and liquidity would remain positive in the stress case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation K12; calculation K20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Thor presents an adequate business profile supported by North American market leadership, a three-way segment split and a low-leverage balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by three years of falling earnings, payouts above free cash flow and contingent dealer obligations. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening, because free cash flow converted only 31.16% of EBITDA. Reported leverage of 1.60x is low in absolute terms, and no peer set or ratings are supplied for comparison with other leveraged issuers. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilising before the facility expires in November 2028 and the notes fall due in October 2029, with the term loan following in November 2030. The primary downside path is a further fall in North American towable demand that deepens operating deleverage while payouts continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the indenture, the proxy statement, covenant certificates, unit-level goodwill headroom and dealer-level repurchase exposure. Top risk: earnings erosion in North American towables combined with payouts above free cash flow.
